clue.text: Starts off puzzle solving slowly, teaser that demands attention

indicators.note: the starts of the four words that follow are taken, one letter from each

explanation.surface: A slow solver is nudged by a tricky puzzle that insists on being noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' looks like it describes the solver, but it tells you to take the opening letters of puzzle, solving, slowly and teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection hissed quietly to catch someone's notice, so it is a sound demanding attention.

clue.text: Set of letters found in post, ultimately

definitions.text: Set of letters found in post, ultimately

parts.words: Set of letters found in post, ultimately
parts.note: the words post and ultimately between them contain O, U, I, A and E, the full group of non-consonant letters

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like letters arriving in the mail, but look at the letters in the words 'post' and 'ultimately': together they supply A, E, I, O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The five letters A, E, I, O and U form the set of sounds made with an open mouth, which is this class of letters.

clue.text: Ponder convoluted tube that's finally manufactured

indicators.note: something convoluted is twisted, so the letters of ponder are twisted into a new order

parts.note: a duct is a tube or pipe carrying fluid

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to think about a twisted pipe that comes out of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convoluted' looks like it describes the tube, but it works only on 'Ponder'; the tube then follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The finished goods that come out at the close of a manufacturing process are its final output.

clue.text: Initially without force, elevating King David, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating lifts a letter higher, so it moves nearer the start
without says a letter is to be dropped from the phrase for initially

parts.note: initially means at first, in the beginning
F is the physics symbol for force
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A tale of King David rising to the throne without using force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes F from AT FIRST, giving ATIRST; 'elevating' then lifts the R up two places in this down entry. The misdirection is King David: the David meant is the French painter Jacques-Louis David.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Louis David was a celebrated French painter, an example of a creative painter.

clue.text: Last short epistle used in university, after appropriate period

indicators.note: the short epistle is used inside the other letters, so it is placed within them

parts.note: something late arrives after the proper time
Tim is short for Timothy, the New Testament letters to Timothy

explanation.surface: A final shortened letter is read at a university after a suitable interval.
explanation.walkthrough: Timothy is one of the New Testament epistles; 'used in' places its short form inside the other letters, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something final, coming at the very end of a series, is the closing one.

clue.text: It's briefly worn by female in dorm, initially

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Something a woman wears for a short while in her dormitory at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' is a pun: the garment is brief, being short.
explanation.definitionFit: A short skirt is a skimpy item worn by women, so 'briefly worn' describes its short length.

clue.text: Is prone to cover up trouble in final sections

indicators.note: one word covers another by wrapping round it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: if one is prone to do something, one tends to
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to hide a problem in the closing parts of a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover up' reads as hiding trouble, but it means one word wraps round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The last parts or remnants of anything are its rear portions, the closing bits.

clue.text: Terminate in small place

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to lay something is to place it down

explanation.surface: An order to finish something off in a tiny location.
explanation.definitionFit: To kill is to end a life, so terminating someone is a violent synonym.

clue.text: Cruel dons trashed patriot in last resort?

indicators.note: trashed means wrecked, so the letters of cruel dons are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Unkind university fellows rubbish a patriot as a final measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Samuel Johnson's remark that patriotism is the last refuge of a scoundrel, so the patriot in last resort is a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's saying makes a rogue who falls back on patriotism the patriot of last resort.

clue.text: Eventually rejecting extremes, everything being considered

indicators.note: rejecting the extremes means throwing away the first and last letters of the word for eventually

parts.note: eventually means finally, in the end

explanation.surface: Someone eventually avoids extreme positions after weighing up everything.
explanation.walkthrough: FINALLY loses its outer letters F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means taking everything into account, as in 'overall' or 'in total'.

clue.text: Prepare on course at Cambridge after first part of tripos, say

indicators.note: after puts the Cambridge word behind the spoken letter
say signals that the letter is to be written as it is spoken

parts.note: the first part of the word tripos is its opening letter, T, written out in full as it is spoken
students are 'up' at a university such as Cambridge while in residence

explanation.surface: A Cambridge student gets ready after the first part of the Tripos, the Cambridge degree exams.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of tripos is T, written out as it is spoken, TEE. 'on course' means on a golf course, not a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf one places the ball on a peg before driving, which is getting ready; figuratively it means to set something up.

clue.text: My reason for being in league to begin with

parts.note: being involved in something is being 'in it'
the setter's 'my' points to the setter, I
one who is in league with you is an ally

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they joined a league at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as a reason: 'in it, I ally' explains being in league.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean at the start, in the first place.

clue.text: Splurge in US city, initially with round of drinks

indicators.note: the city comes first, with the round of drinks after it

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a shout is one's turn to buy a round, in British and Australian slang

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a spending spree in an American city, starting by buying everyone drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shout' is British slang for a turn to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money extravagantly is a colloquial sense of the phrase, as in to splash out.

clue.text: Optical device initially put together, first patented in 1960

definitions.text: Optical device initially put together, first patented in 1960

parts.words: Optical device initially put together, first patented in 1960
parts.note: the name is built from the initials of Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation, a device first patented around 1960

explanation.walkthrough: 'initially put together' says the word is made from the initial letters of a phrase, Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: This optical device, emitting a narrow intense beam, dates from 1960 and its name is an acronym.

clue.text: Initial combination that's familiar in a mass

indicators.note: in places the familiar friend inside the letters for a mass

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
a familiar is a close friend or crony

explanation.surface: A friend familiar to everyone in a crowd joins the mix at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: CRONY goes between A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from the first letters of other words is a combination of initials.

clue.text: Regions are originally subject to new order

indicators.note: originally can mean inventively, in an original way, so the letters of regions are are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Territories are first put under a new regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letters signal, but here it means inventively and rearranges REGIONS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange or restructure something is to put it into a fresh arrangement.

clue.text: Ship's officer died, finished off on board

parts.note: a mate is an officer on a merchant ship
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A ship's officer died, killed on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship but means a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a king checkmated is beaten, finished off on the board.

clue.text: First characters assembled in military mess

definitions.text: First characters assembled in military mess

parts.words: First characters assembled in military mess
parts.note: the word is made from the opening letters of the soldiers' phrase Situation Normal: All Fouled Up

explanation.walkthrough: The word is formed from the first letters of a soldiers' phrase, politely 'Situation Normal, All Fouled Up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Army slang for a chaotic blunder, built from the initials of a weary soldiers' saying.

clue.text: Almost ended within a social function, primarily

indicators.note: within puts the shortened word inside the a-plus-dance letters

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance, a social function

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for ended is dropped

parts.note: something ended is over

explanation.surface: A party nearly finished during a social event at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final letter of the word for ended; 'within' puts what remains between the A and the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means most importantly, first and foremost.

clue.text: Charge making sense with pound discounted at the end

indicators.note: discounted means left out, and at the end says it is the final letter that goes

parts.note: to sense something is to feel it
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A price that seems reasonable once a pound is knocked off at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discounted' sounds like a price cut but means L is dropped from FEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment demanded for a service is a charge, as in a lawyer's bill.

clue.text: Once in fashion, near the beginning, but not first of all

parts.note: to fashion something is to form it

indicators.note: but not says a letter is to be taken out of the word for near the beginning

parts.note: early means near the start of a period

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something once in style near the start, but not first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' is not a phrase meaning initially: it is the first letter of the word 'all', which 'but not' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at an earlier time, in the past.

clue.text: Where shooting happens, for a start

definitions.meaning: films are shot in a studio setting, on a film set
a beginning, as in the beginning of an illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' suggests guns but means filming. Read as two words the answer says where filming happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, such as an illness or winter, is its first arrival.

clue.text: Schedule disrupted by old male calling at first light

indicators.note: the schedule is broken open by the letter for old placed within it

parts.note: a roster is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A timetable thrown out by an old man phoning at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male calling' looks like a man on the phone; it is a cockerel crowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock bird crows at dawn, so it is the male that calls at first light.

clue.text: Pull lass back who's last in line?

indicators.note: back says the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drag is to pull
a gal is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: Tugging a girl back, she being the last in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAG plus GAL read backwards gives LAG plus GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler who falls behind ends up at the back of a queue.

clue.text: Like final person appearing, having left a big game

parts.note: a test is a Test match, a major international cricket or rugby game

explanation.surface: Someone who turned up last has left a major match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent arrival is the newest, so the final person appearing is this one.

clue.text: Redesigned faster course one finally enjoys

indicators.note: something redesigned is rebuilt in a new shape, so the letters of faster are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racetrack rebuilt to be quicker that a driver finally enjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a racetrack; it is a course of a meal. Afters is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The pudding or dessert is the meal's final course, eaten after the main.

clue.text: First in college, learner with highest place — being this?

definitions.text: First in college, learner with highest place — being this?

indicators.note: first in takes the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: L is the learner's sign, as on a British learner driver's plate
Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A student top of the college class must be the brightest.
explanation.walkthrough: A learner who takes a First and the highest place is the brainiest, so the whole clue defines too.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first and highest among students marks the most intelligent of them.

clue.text: First or last word from Italian in Chicago, oddly

definitions.text: First or last word from Italian

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in the odd positions of the word Chicago

explanation.surface: An Italian in Chicago starts or ends a speech with a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: C, I, A and O are letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian greeting means both hello and goodbye, so it is the first or last word said.

clue.text: Affluence in some areas, eventually

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wealth arrives in parts of the country in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable wealth means living without money worries, as in 'a life of comfort'.

clue.text: Like celebrity, observed to end badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of to end are put together in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A star who was seen coming to a sad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed' is a second definition of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is famous and well known, so to be like one is to be distinguished.

clue.text: Miserable kind of clue this ultimately is

definitions.text: kind of clue this ultimately is
definitions.meaning: this clue is the very last of the clues in the vertical list

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to the clue itself, the final clue in its column.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or depressed is a colloquial sense, as in 'feeling a bit blue'.

clue.text: Ultimately failing to reach time for world record?

indicators.note: failing to reach the end means the final letter is not got to, so it drops off

parts.note: ultimately means at last, in the end

explanation.surface: A runner finally falls short of the time needed for a world record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world record' sounds like athletics, but it is a book recording the world: a book of maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps records the whole world, which makes it a world record.

clue.text: Concluding provocation upset stalwarts

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of stalwarts are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Loyal supporters are angered by a final insult.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from the straw that broke the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The final irritation that pushes someone past their limit is the last in a series of provocations.
